Definition: from G2818; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively):--be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance).
KeyPassages: Matthew 5:5; Mark 10:17; Luke 10:25; 1 Corinthians 6:9; Galatians 4:30; Hebrews 1:4
BiblicalUsage: Kleronomeo means to be an heir, to inherit. Matthew 5:5 promises the meek shall inherit the earth, Mark 10:17 and Luke 10:25 both ask, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life, 1 Corinthians 6:9 warns the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God, Galatians 4:30 says the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman, and Hebrews 1:4 says Christ hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than the angels.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe inheritance in the Bible is always by promise, never by wages: the meek inherit the earth because God gives it, and the unrighteous do not inherit because God withholds it. I hold that the question in Mark 10:17 and Luke 10:25 is the question every man must answer, and the answer is the Son who inherited the excellent name.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Mark; Luke; 1 Corinthians; Galatians; Hebrews
